data.checking-a-deployment#Checking a deploym: A deployed relay can be proven end to end without an OpenID Connect login.
data.mint-credentials#Mint credentials on the:
On the host, mint short-lived credentials with the keyring turnd uses (the first --turn-secret-file signs; the TTL is capped at 1h). The username is printed; the password goes to a new 0600 file, never to stdout or the command line:
turnd mint-credentials --turn-secret-file /etc/turnd/turn.secret \ --subject probe --ttl 10m --password-out ./probe.pw # prints :.probe
data.reading-the-result#Reading the result:
PASS turn:turn.example.org:3478?transport=udp mapped=198.51.100.7:51234 relay-a=203.0.113.5:49160 relay-b=203.0.113.5:49161 roundtrip=3ms FAIL turns:turn.example.org:443?transport=tcp stage=connect: tls: failed to verify certificate: ... One line per server, PASS or FAIL with the stage that failed: connect, binding, allocate, permission, relay A->B, relay B->A. The exit status is 1 if any failed.
--realm is turnd’s --realm; a mismatch is reported at allocate.
data.turnprobe#Run turnprobe:
From anywhere that can reach the relay, run turnprobe. For each --server it sends a STUN Binding (printing the mapped address), opens two allocations, permits each other’s relayed address, and sends a datagram from relay A to relay B and back; that proves relaying, with nothing else needed. A turns: certificate is verified against the system roots with SNI set to the host.
go install github.com/go-turn/turn/cmd/turnprobe@latest turnprobe --username '1763400000:ab12.probe' --password-file ./probe.pw \ --realm turn.example.org \ --server 'turn:turn.example.org:3478?transport=udp' \ --server 'turn:turn.example.org:3478?transport=tcp' \ --server 'turns:turn.example.org:443?transport=tcp'

data.after-deploying#After deploying: Prove the relay end to end without an OpenID Connect login: Checking a deployment.
data.deploying#Deploying:
One host, one binary:
CGO_ENABLED=0 go install github.com/go-turn/turn/cmd/turnd@latest
data.ports#Ports:
Open these at the host firewall and at the cloud security group:
port for UDP 3478 STUN and TURN over UDP (--stun-listen :3478) TCP 3478 TURN over TCP (--turn-tcp-listen :3478) TCP 5349 TURN over TLS (--turns-listen :5349), for networks that block UDP UDP range relayed addresses (--relay-port-min 49160 --relay-port-max 49999) TCP 443 HTTPS: /login, /callback, /grpc, through the host’s reverse proxy to --listen 127.0.0.1:8080 (the proxy must pass WebSocket upgrades) To share 443 between that HTTPS site and TURN over TLS, see TURN over TLS on 443.
data.secrets#Secrets:
Every secret is a file, refused when world-readable; none is a flag value or an environment variable. Make them readable by the service account only:
flag content --session-key-file 32+ random bytes --turn-secret-file 16+ random bytes --client-secret-file the issuer’s client secret Repeat --session-key-file / --turn-secret-file to rotate: the first signs, the others only verify.
data.the-http-half#The HTTP half: turnd --issuer https://login.example.org --client-id turnd \ --client-secret-file /etc/turnd/client-secret \ --session-key-file /etc/turnd/session.key \ --turn-secret-file /etc/turnd/turn.secret \ --allowed-origin https://go-tex.github.io \ --public-url https://turn.example.org --listen 127.0.0.1:8080 \ --turn-uri 'turns:turn.example.org:443?transport=tcp' Register /callback as the client’s redirect URI at the issuer (the one named by --client-id).
data.the-relay#The relay:
turnd starts the relay when a listen flag is set:
flag --relay-ip required; --relay-advertise-ip behind a NAT --stun-listen :3478 STUN and TURN over UDP --turn-tcp-listen :3478 TURN over TCP --turns-listen :443 TURN over TLS, with --tls-cert-file and --tls-key-file --relay-port-min / --relay-port-max the range of relayed UDP ports --proxy-protocol-from repeatable; accept a PROXY protocol v2 header on TCP and TLS connections from that prefix The relay’s credential hook is the keyring’s Auth, so the minted :. usernames are what it accepts (the tag says which of the rotating secrets signed it).

data.http#HTTP, for browser navigations:
Only browser navigations stay HTTP:
HTTP GET /login?origin= starts the OIDC login (code + PKCE) in a popup; an origin not in --allowed-origin is a 400, never a redirect GET /callback page that postMessages {type:"turnd-session",token,expires} (or {type:"turnd-error",error}) to window.opener, target origin = the allowlisted one GET /healthz ok
data.rpcs#RPCs: RPC token returns Credentials session, or issuer access token IceServers{ice_servers[{urls,username,credential}], ttl} CreateRoom session or access token {room, peer:"host", token, expires}; the room ID is 128 random bits JoinRoom{room,name} none: the room ID {peer, host, token, expires, pending:true}; the guest is pending Admit{room,peer} / Deny{room,peer} host token admit a pending guest / refuse it (or remove an admitted one): its token is dead RoomCredentials{room} an admitted peer’s token IceServers expiring with the room, charged to the host CloseRoom{room} host token ends the room Room(stream Envelope) returns (stream Envelope) peer token + x-turn-room metadata the room’s one stream: events down, messages up; ending it is leaving What the room RPCs mean is in Rooms and admission.
data.status-codes#Status codes:
A message that breaks the protocol (too large, a spoofed from, a bad kind, a pending sender, guest to guest) ends the sender’s stream with a status: RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, PERMISSION_DENIED, INVALID_ARGUMENT. Other refusals:
status when UNAUTHENTICATED no or dead token NOT_FOUND ALREADY_EXISTS a second stream for one peer FAILED_PRECONDITION already admitted UNAVAILABLE server full
data.the-go-client#The Go client:
For the browser and native: github.com/go-turn/turn/rendezvous/client. Create, Join(name) (blocks until admitted, ErrDenied otherwise), Admit, Deny, Send, Recv, Credentials, Close.
It is a real grpc-go client dialed over the browser’s WebSocket through syscall/js. It adds about 16 MB to a wasm binary (3.5 MB more gzipped), almost all of it grpc. go-crdt/collab’s js/wasm build does not link grpc, so a page that does not otherwise ship it should load this client in a separate wasm, fetched when a collaboration starts.
data.the-grpc-api#The gRPC API: The API is gRPC, proto/turn/v1/turnd.proto (service turn.v1.Turnd). The generated code is committed, and CI regenerates it and fails on a diff.
data.tokens#Tokens: A token travels as authorization: Bearer … metadata, never in a URL.
data.transport#Transport:
A plain grpc.Server is served over a WebSocket at /grpc (grpc-transports/websocket), which is what a browser can speak, including the bidirectional stream.
The WebSocket upgrade enforces the exact origin allowlist (--allowed-origin; scheme and port included). A client with no Origin header is a native client.

data.creds-and-session#creds and session: creds is the credential scheme and its keyring (the TURN REST API usernames :.); session verifies the session token a login produces.
data.packages#Packages: The module is github.com/go-turn/turn. Besides the turnd and turnprobe commands it has these packages.
data.rendezvous-client#rendezvous/client: The Go client for the rooms; see The gRPC API.
data.server#server:
The RFC 8656 TURN server: UDP relayed transport, reached over UDP, TCP or TLS (the caller passes the sockets), plus the STUN Binding answer. Long-term credentials (MD5, and SHA-256 when the client asks) with NONCE expiry (438); permissions last 300 s, channels 600 s.
srv, err := server.New(server.Config{ Realm: "turn.example.org", Auth: func(username string) (password string, ok bool) { /* wrap creds.Verify */ }, RelayIP: netip.MustParseAddr("203.0.113.5"), }) go srv.ServePacketConn(udpConn) // UDP clients go srv.ServeListener(tcpListener) // TCP clients go srv.ServeTLS(tcpListener443, tlsCfg) // turns: What the server refuses to relay to, and its bounds, are in the Security policy.
interop/ is the judge: github.com/pion/turn/v4 (test-only) allocates, permits, binds a channel and round-trips data through the server over UDP and TCP. go test -bench . ./server prints allocations/s and relayed packets/s; the comparison with coturn on one core is still to do.
data.stun#stun:
The RFC 8489 message codec with the RFC 8656 TURN attributes and ChannelData framing. Decoding is strict and bounded: it refuses a length that overruns the datagram, framing that is not 4-aligned, and more than MaxAttributes (64) attributes; attributes after MESSAGE-INTEGRITY are not visible.
It covers MESSAGE-INTEGRITY (HMAC-SHA1), MESSAGE-INTEGRITY-SHA256, FINGERPRINT, the long-term key derivations (MD5 and SHA-256) and USERHASH. Tested against the RFC 5769 vectors (decode, verify, byte-identical re-encode); FuzzDecode and FuzzChannelData have a committed seed corpus under stun/testdata/fuzz. SASLprep (OpaqueString) is the caller’s job.

data.deciding#Deciding: call by effect Admit{room,peer} the host admits a pending guest Deny{room,peer} the host refuses a pending guest, or removes an admitted one: its token is dead RoomCredentials{room} an admitted peer IceServers expiring with the room, charged to the host CloseRoom{room} the host ends the room
data.knocking#Knocking, not entering:
A leaked room link lets a stranger knock, not enter. The room ID is 128 random bits, and a guest who joins with it is pending:
a pending guest only receives: it cannot send and cannot get credentials; it counts against a separate pending cap, and a pending TTL; the host sees sys.knock (from = the guest, body = its display name, at most 64 characters, no control characters) and decides. Only admitted guests count against --max-guests and produce sys.join.
data.protocol-breaks#What breaks the protocol: A message that is too large, a spoofed from, a bad kind, one sent by a pending guest, or one from guest to guest ends the sender’s stream with a status (RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, PERMISSION_DENIED, INVALID_ARGUMENT); see The gRPC API.
data.rooms-and-admission#Rooms and admission: A room is how two peers meet with one link: a host opens it, shares the link, and the guest’s answer comes back on its own.
data.system-events#System events:
Delivered on the room’s one stream (Room), events down, messages up:
event sys.knock a guest is pending sys.admitted sys.denied sys.join an admitted guest joined sys.leave sys.closed the room ended sys.error a message the other peer could not take; the stream stays open Ending the stream is leaving. A second stream for one peer is refused with ALREADY_EXISTS.

data.bounds#Bounds:
All in server.Config: allocations per user and in total, lifetime cap, per-allocation byte rate, relay port range, permissions and channels per allocation, concurrent connections, idle and handshake timeouts, datagram size.
Permissions last 300 s and channels 600 s. Long-term credentials use NONCE expiry (438).
data.origins-and-tokens#Browser origins and t: The WebSocket upgrade enforces the exact origin allowlist, scheme and port included. /login with an origin that is not allowed is a 400, never a redirect. /callback posts the session only to the allowlisted origin. A token is authorization: Bearer … metadata, never a URL.
data.proxy-protocol#PROXY protocol: A PROXY header is accepted only from the prefixes given to --proxy-protocol-from; a header from any other source is never honoured, and a connection from a listed prefix without a valid header is closed.
data.relay-address-policy#The relay does not:
By default the server never relays to or from:
loopback, 0.0.0.0/8, RFC 1918, 100.64/10; link-local (169.254.169.254 included), multicast, ULA; the NAT64, 6to4 and Teredo forms, and IPv4-mapped forms of those; its own addresses. It answers 403. The one exception is two clients relaying to each other: an own address is a peer only at the relayed port of a live allocation. That is checked when the permission or channel is made and again on every datagram, which is handed over in memory, so SSH, 443 and the TURN listeners stay unreachable through the relay.
Config.AllowPeers re-enables ranges (the tests use 127.0.0.0/8).
data.reporting#Reporting a vulnerability: Report privately through GitHub’s private vulnerability reporting, from the Security tab of go-turn/turn; do not open a public issue for it. In scope: turnd, the relay policy, the credentials and the rendezvous. Only the latest minor version is supported. The full policy is SECURITY.md in that repository.
data.rooms#Rooms: A leaked room link lets a stranger knock, not enter; see Rooms and admission.
data.secrets#Secrets: Every secret is a file, refused when world-readable; none is a flag value or an environment variable. Secrets rotate by repeating the flag: the first signs, the others only verify.
data.security-policy#Security policy: What turnd refuses to do, as stated by the project.
data.untrusted-input#Untrusted input: The stun decoder is strict and bounded: it refuses a length that overruns the datagram, framing that is not 4-aligned, and more than MaxAttributes (64) attributes. FuzzDecode and FuzzChannelData have a committed seed corpus under stun/testdata/fuzz; CI also fuzzes the PROXY header parser, the credential parser and keyring, and the session verifier.

data.build-caddy#Build Caddy: xcaddy build --with github.com/mholt/caddy-l4@v0.1.3 The version is pinned because caddy-l4 calls itself experimental.
data.the-caddyfile#The Caddyfile: { servers :443 { listener_wrappers { layer4 { @turn tls sni turn.example.org route @turn { tls proxy { proxy_protocol v2 upstream tcp/127.0.0.1:3478 } } } tls } } } # A site block makes Caddy obtain the certificate that the `tls` handler above # presents for turn.example.org. turn.example.org { respond "turnd relay" 200 }
data.turn-over-tls-on-443#TURN over TLS on 44: TURN over TLS can share 443 with the HTTPS site when Caddy demultiplexes by SNI with caddy-l4. Caddy terminates TLS for turn.example.org itself and proxies plain TCP to turnd with a PROXY protocol v2 header, so turnd still sees the real client address (XOR-MAPPED-ADDRESS, quotas and logs).
data.what-has-been-tested#What has been teste:
The Caddyfile follows caddy-l4’s docs/examples/combining_apps.md; it has not been run against a Caddy by the project, only the header handling is tested (with pion’s TCP client behind a proxy that prepends a v2 header).
The separate --turns-listen (TLS handled by turnd, port 5349 or 443 on a second address) stays available for a host without Caddy; there the PROXY header, if any, precedes the ClientHello.
data.what-the-proxy-header-allows#What the PR: The header is accepted only from the listed prefixes: a connection from one of them without a valid header is closed, and a header from any other source is never honoured.
